items.q: Write the set of even numbers less than 10.
hints: List every even number that is less than 10, in curly brackets.
Even numbers less than 10: 2, 4, 6, 8.

items.q: Is 3 in the set {1,2,4}?
hints: Check whether the number appears as an element of the set.
The set {1,2,4} contains 1, 2, and 4 — not 3.
No

items.q: List the set of prime numbers less than 8.
hints: List every prime number (only two factors: 1 and itself) less than 8.
Primes less than 8: 2, 3, 5, 7.

items.q: What brackets are used for a set?
hints: Recall the standard notation used to write down a set.
Sets are written inside { }.
Curly brackets

items.q: Is {a,e,i,o,u} a set?
hints: A set is any well-defined collection of distinct elements.
{a,e,i,o,u} is a well-defined collection of distinct letters (the vowels).
Yes

items.q: Can a set contain repeated elements?
hints: Recall the key property that distinguishes a set from a list.
A set only records whether an element is present, not how many times.
No

items.q: List the set of factors of 12.
hints: List every whole number that divides 12 exactly.
1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12 all divide into 12 with no remainder.

items.q: If U = {1,2,3,4,5,6}, find the complement of {1,3,5}.
hints: The complement is every element of U that is NOT in the given set.
Check whether the number appears as an element of U.
U only goes up to 10, so 11 is not listed.
No

items.q: True or false: every set A discussed in a question is a subset of U.
hints: Recall what the universal set U represents.
U contains every element under consideration, so any set A in the question is drawn from within it.
True

items.q: If U = {a,b,c,d} and A = {a,c}, find A'.
items.imageAlt: A universal set U containing a, b, c, d. Set A (circle) contains a and c. The shaded region outside A represents A', unknown.
items.imageCaption: Shaded: outside A, inside U. A' = ?
hints: The complement A' is every element of U that is NOT in A.
U = {a,b,c,d}, remove a, c.
{b,d}

items.q: What does the universal set represent?
hints: Recall the definition of U in set theory.
U is the set containing everything relevant to the current problem.
All elements being considered
The complement B' is every element of U that is NOT in B.
Find A' first, then take the complement of that result.
A' = {1,3,5,7}, and the complement of A' brings you back to A.

items.q: If A = {1,2,3} and B = {3,4,5}, find A n B.
items.imageAlt: Two overlapping circles A (1,2) and B (4,5) with 3 in the overlap, shaded, representing A ∩ B, unknown.
hints: The intersection A n B contains only the elements in BOTH sets.
A = {1,2,3}, B = {3,4,5} — the only shared element is 3.

items.q: If A = {1,2,3} and B = {3,4,5}, find A u B.
items.imageAlt: Two overlapping circles A (1,2) and B (4,5) with 3 in the overlap, both circles shaded, representing A ∪ B, unknown.
hints: The union A u B contains every element that is in A OR B (no repeats).
Combine {1,2,3} and {3,4,5}, listing 3 only once.

items.q: If A and B have no common elements, what is A n B?
hints: The intersection contains only elements shared by both sets.
With no elements in common, nothing belongs to the intersection.

items.q: If A = {2,4,6} and B = {4,6,8}, find A n B.
hints: The intersection A n B contains only the elements in BOTH sets.
A = {2,4,6}, B = {4,6,8} — the shared elements are 4 and 6.

items.q: If A = {a,b} and B = {b,c,d}, find A u B.
hints: The union A u B contains every element that is in A OR B (no repeats).
Combine {a,b} and {b,c,d}, listing b only once.
{a,b,c,d}

items.q: What word describes two sets with empty intersection?
hints: Recall the term for sets that share no elements.
When A n B = {}, the sets have no overlap.
Disjoint
Find the elements that appear in all three sets at once.
Only 4 is in A, B, and C.

items.q: In a class of 30, 18 like maths, 12 like physics, and 7 like both. How many like maths only?
items.imageAlt: A Venn diagram for a class of 30. Maths (18 total) and Physics (12 total) circles overlap with 7 in both. Maths only is unknown.
hints: Maths only = total who like maths, minus those who like both.

items.q: In the same class, how many like neither subject?
hints: First find how many like at least one subject, then subtract from the class total.
Maths only (11) + physics only (12-7=5) + both (7) = 23 like at least one, so 30 - 23.

items.q: How many like at least one subject?
hints: Add maths only, physics only, and both together.
11 (maths only) + 5 (physics only) + 7 (both).

items.q: A Venn diagram has 5 in A only, 3 in both, and 4 in B only. How many are in A?
hints: The whole of set A is 'A only' plus the overlap with B.

items.q: If 20 are in U, 6 in A only, 5 in both, and 3 in B only, how many are outside both?
hints: First add up everyone inside A or B, then subtract from the total in U.
6 + 5 + 3 = 14 inside A or B, so 20 - 14.

items.q: What does the overlap in a Venn diagram represent?
hints: Recall which set operation corresponds to the shared region of two circles.
The region common to both circles contains elements in both A and B.
Intersection
